tutorial.speaker: hassan
tutorial.text: Welcome to mission control! I'm Dr. Hassan Nasr, your flight director. Today we design a satellite to watch over the Nile Delta's farms and water.

tutorial.speaker: hassan
tutorial.text: These seven meters are your limits. Every choice moves several of them at once — that's real mission design.

tutorial.speaker: hassan
tutorial.text: Your Mission Commander picks the orbit, the mission length and the rocket. A sun-synchronous orbit gives the same lighting every day — perfect for comparing crops.

tutorial.speaker: hassan
tutorial.text: Each rocket lifts a certain mass to each orbit. Heavier spacecraft need bigger, pricier rockets.

tutorial.speaker: hassan
tutorial.text: The Science Lead chooses instruments. Each one adds science — and also mass, power, cost and data.

tutorial.speaker: hassan
tutorial.text: Hover over the Thermal Infrared Imager. See the meters preview the change before you even click?

tutorial.speaker: hassan
tutorial.text: The Spacecraft Engineer feeds the instruments: solar arrays for power, a battery for the shadow, propellant for keeping the orbit.

tutorial.speaker: hassan
tutorial.text: If the load is higher than generation, instruments switch off. Keep at least 15% margin — arrays weaken every year.

tutorial.speaker: hassan
tutorial.text: Data is worthless until it reaches Earth. The Comms Officer picks the radio and the ground stations.

tutorial.speaker: hassan
tutorial.text: Our starter S-band radio cannot keep up with the imager. Try the X-band transmitter and watch this turn green.

tutorial.speaker: hassan
tutorial.text: When you're ready, open the readiness review. Red means NO-GO — read why, fix it, then sign off.

tutorial.speaker: hassan
tutorial.text: Then launch! Surprises will happen during the mission. Choose wisely — and remember, there's no single perfect design.

intro_nile_watch.speaker: hassan
intro_nile_watch.text: The Nile Delta feeds millions, and water is precious. A satellite that sees crop health can tell farmers where to irrigate.

intro_nile_watch.speaker: hassan
intro_nile_watch.text: We need a multispectral imager or a camera, at least two years in orbit. The budget is modest — spend wisely.

intro_storm_watch.speaker: hassan
intro_storm_watch.text: Dust storms and flash floods can strike in hours. Forecasters need eyes that never blink.

intro_storm_watch.speaker: hassan
intro_storm_watch.text: Carry a sounder or a thermal imager and watch for five years. Which orbit lets you stare at one region all the time?

intro_ice_hunter.speaker: hassan
intro_ice_hunter.text: Future crews will need water on the Moon — to drink, to breathe, even to make rocket fuel.

intro_ice_hunter.speaker: hassan
intro_ice_hunter.text: Bring a neutron spectrometer to sniff out hydrogen, plus an altimeter or thermal imager to map the craters. Deep-space comms are a must.

intro_red_relay.speaker: hassan
intro_red_relay.text: Two jobs at once: study the Martian air, and relay data for the rovers below.

intro_red_relay.speaker: hassan
intro_red_relay.text: Mars is far: weak sunlight, a 12-minute radio delay, and launch windows every 26 months. Miss it and we wait two years.

intro_first_light.speaker: hassan
intro_first_light.text: We want light that left the first galaxies 13 billion years ago. It arrives as faint infrared heat.

intro_first_light.speaker: hassan
intro_first_light.text: An infrared telescope must be very cold and very steady. Somewhere far from Earth's warmth would be ideal…

intro_sandbox.speaker: hassan
intro_sandbox.text: Sandbox mode: no limits. Build anything and see what happens.

intro_sandbox.speaker: hassan
intro_sandbox.text: Try extremes. No battery? A giant radar on a tiny bus? The report will tell you why.

council_solo.speaker: hassan
council_solo.text: The agency gives you {budget}. Here is a suggested split between your four roles — adjust it if you like.

launch_nogo.speaker: hassan
launch_nogo.text: We still have NO-GO items. Launching now will probably end badly. Are you sure?

launch_go.speaker: hassan
launch_go.text: All stations GO. Good luck, crew!

report_success.speaker: hassan
report_success.text: Mission accomplished! Read the report — even a success has lessons.

report_partial.speaker: hassan
report_partial.text: We got some science home, but not everything. Let's see what to change.

report_failure.speaker: hassan
report_failure.text: Every space agency has lost missions. What matters is understanding why — let's read the report.

review_cml4.speaker: hassan
review_cml4.text: Point design reached: CML 4. This concept is mature enough to fly.

review_cml3.speaker: hassan
review_cml3.text: We're still exploring the trade space. Turn the yellows green before we commit.

review_cml2.speaker: hassan
review_cml2.text: This is still an early feasibility sketch. Let's fix the red items first.

twin_intro.speaker: hassan
twin_intro.text: Your design is a close cousin of a real mission:

priya_tip.speaker: priya
priya_tip.text: Ground station here! We can only listen while your spacecraft is in view. A faster radio or a bigger network gets more of your data home.
